items.body: The grand final for Australia’s National Rugby League won’t have an entertainment spot after talks with Tones And I fell through due to scheduling conflicts. Tones (real name: Toni Watson) had been tipped as the headline music act for the NRL’s showpiece event, set for Sunday, Oct. 4 at Sydney’s Accor Stadium. That won’t happen, her reps say. And the league won’t pursue another artist to fill the void. According to a statement from Tones’ team at Lemon Tree Management, the singer was “recently approached to perform the preshow at the NRL Grand Final.” An offer was presented to Tones via management on Sept. 5, reads the message, seen by Billboard .  “Tones had a prior commitment with Macklemore in America and explored all avenues to make it work.” However, “nothing was signed or confirmed in writing.”  “Due to the last minute nature,” the statement continues, “and prior commitments by Tones, we were unable to accept the offer. We wish the NRL nothing but the very best for their event.” The league has said it will, instead, funnel that budget towards sports programs for underprivileged children. It was acquired at Oukaïmeden Observatory in Morocco with approximately 200 hours of observations and shows a large patch of the sky, equivalent to the area of one thousand full moons tiled together, in the constellation of Auriga (the charioteer ). From left to right, the five supernova remnants visible across the field are G181.1+9.5 , G182.4+4.3 , G179.0+2.6 , G180.0−1.7 (Sh2-240, the Spaghetti Nebula ), and G178.2−4.2 . They are highlighted in the annotated image , together with open cluster M37 and the Tadpole Nebula . As each explosion expanded into space , it created a growing shell of shocked gas and delicate filamentary structures shown in red ( hydrogen ) and blue ( oxygen ), respectively. items.summary: Will the K-pop megahit take the lead? We'll soon see.
items.body: KPop Demon Hunters has slayed on Billboard ’s Top Soundtracks chart, having led the list for 61 weeks – just one week shy of the record. This chart was introduced a little more than 25 years ago – on June 30, 2001 – which means it doesn’t include blockbuster soundtracks of previous eras, such as West Side Story, The Sound of Music, Doctor Zhivago, Saturday Night Fever and Purple Rain . Actually, it does include one – The Vince Guaraldi Trio ’s 1965 TV soundtrack, A Charlie Brown Christmas – but only because of its chart success since 2001. KPop Demon Hunters has been No. 1 for all but four of its 65 weeks on Top Soundtracks, having yielded for one week each to Wicked: For Good , the holiday perennial A Charlie Brown Christmas , Charli xcx ’s Wuthering Heights and the soundtrack to this year’s most-talked about TV miniseries, Heated Rivalry . items.title: Qualcomm is solving Snapdragon X’s Linux problem
items.summary: Bringing this powerful operating system to the very latest in mobile computing hardware.
items.body: TL;DR Qualcomm shares that Snapdragon X-series laptops are getting Linux support. Debian compatibility should roll out sometime later in 2026. Ubuntu is planning support for Snapdragon X2 devices early next year. It’s taken a couple decades, but something big has finally started happening for how we get computing done on laptops. After years of trying to be tiny desktop computers, running the same kind of chips that were never really designed for power efficiency, laptops began broadly embracing RISC computing — including models built around Qualcomm Snapdragon chips like the X series . This week at Qualcomm’s annual Snapdragon Summit, the company is sharing news of a big new upgrade for such models that power users are really going to love. For all the speed and battery life they offer, Snapdragon laptops have had at least one big blind spot: Linux. Even though different Snapdragon chips have been powering Android (with its deep Linux roots) devices for ages, initial Snapdragon X laptops lacked support for mainstream Linux distros .

items.body: TL;DR Google’s Android boss says growing interest in foldables could give developers more reason to optimize their apps for larger screens. Some Android apps still haven’t properly adapted to foldables, but Google says developers are either working on improvements or talking with the company. Apple’s iPhone Duo could expand the foldable audience enough to encourage better app experiences across both iOS and Android. Android foldables have spent years getting the hardware right, but the app problem has been much harder to shake. Apple’s arrival with the iPhone Duo could finally give developers another reason to take foldable layouts seriously, and Google’s Android boss thinks Android users could benefit too. Speaking to Tom’s Guide , Android Ecosystem President Sameer Samat said developers see more value in investing in foldables as the form factor becomes more popular. items.title: Blame this Google Maps Android Auto bug for your next speeding ticket
items.summary: Google Maps' speedometer is swapping between MPH and KPH for some users
items.body: TL;DR Multiple users have reported that Google Maps’ speedometer is switching from MPH to KPH (or vice versa). The issue seems to primarily affect Android Auto, but at least one user reports a similar experience on the mobile app. It’s not currently clear why this is happening or how widespread the issue is. One of Google Maps’ useful features is that the app can show both the posted speed limit on the street where you’re driving and the speed you’re currently traveling, as calculated by GPS. This week, though, many users are reporting that Google Maps on Android Auto is bungling that feature in a strange way. In a Reddit thread (as spotted by Auto Evolution ), four users all say that the speedometer in Google Maps on Android Auto has started alternating between miles per hour and kilometers per hour, irrespective of their own settings. One user even says they’re experiencing the same issue in Google Maps on their phone.

items.title: Gemini just got a big upgrade with new connected apps for work, creativity, and life
items.summary: You can now plug Airtable, Adobe, Peloton, and more directly into Google Gemini.
items.body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Gemini is getting several new connected apps. Some of these new connected apps include Airtable, Adobe, Peloton, and SeatGeek. These tools are rolling out starting today. Google continues to expand Gemini’s capabilities, not only through updates, but also by integrating new services through connected apps. Most recently , the tech giant expanded the AI’s connected app ecosystem to include services such as iHeartRadio, Zocdoc, Ticketmaster, and more. Now, get ready for another wave of new connected apps coming our way. If you’re unfamiliar with connected Gemini apps, these are apps that can connect with Gemini. They allow you to access those services as you converse with the chatbot. This way, you don’t have to leave your conversation to switch over to a new tab to perform other tasks, like getting tickets to an event.

items.body: A photo of the Dynamic Aviation A200 aircraft, which will conduct low-flying research flights over farmland near Greeley, Colorado, to measure emissions in October 2026. Dynamic Aviation Agricultural emissions represent an important and understudied part of Earth’s land and atmosphere systems. The FarmFlux mission will deploy more than a dozen sensors to measure ozone, methane, ammonia, particulates, and other pollutants rising from agricultural lands and animal farms and the interaction with the Earth’s atmosphere. The mission is jointly led by NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland; Colorado State University; and Boston University.  The Colorado deployment is the first series of flights for the FarmFlux mission. Additional low-altitude research flights are scheduled over farmland in Amarillo, Texas, from late October to early November. For the March to July 2027 growing season, research flights with a NASA P-3 Orion aircraft are scheduled in the Midwest and California’s Central Valley with a focus on croplands.  For more information about the FarmFlux mission, visit: https://espo.nasa.gov/farmflux By Sharon Teitelba…

items.body: An image from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope of galaxy cluster MACS J0417 is part of repeated observations to monitor for the reappearance of supernova Athena, which can help astronomers measure the expansion rate of the universe. NASA, ESA, STScI, M. Pascale (UCLA); Image Processing: J. DePasquale (STScI) NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope captured this image of massive galaxy cluster MACS J0417 (left of center) on Sept. 19, 2026. This galaxy cluster acts as a gravitational lens , bending and magnifying light from objects far behind it. Supernova Athena, discovered by NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope in 2025, is predicted to reappear between now and early March 2027. Measuring the timing of Athena’s reappearances can help researchers map the mass of MACS J0417, which acts as a magnifying, foreground lens for distant objects, and refine our understanding of the expansion rate of the universe. Hubble also completed its 200,000th orbit around Earth on Sept. 19, marking another new milestone for an observatory that continues to transform our understanding of the universe. items.title: YouTube is finally giving you more control over what shows up on your Home feed
items.summary: You'll be able to save separate feeds for different interests, moods, and routines.
items.body: TL;DR YouTube is turning its earlier Custom Feed experiment into a full feature that lets you build recommendation feeds with conversational prompts. You can save multiple feeds for different interests, moods, or routines, and YouTube will keep them updated with fresh recommendations. Custom Feeds are coming soon to users in the US across mobile, web, and TVs. YouTube’s Home tab has always had a funny way of overreacting. Watch one random woodworking video, and suddenly the algorithm can decide you’ve found your new life’s calling. Last year, YouTube started testing a way to fight that problem by letting some users tell an AI chatbot what they actually wanted to see. Now that experiment is growing up, with YouTube officially announcing Custom Feeds, giving viewers a more direct way to build separate recommendation feeds around specific interests, routines, or moods. The original test added a “Your Custom Feed” chip beside Home for select users. You could prompt YouTube to adjust what appeared there, essentially correcting the recommendation algorithm instead of waiting for your watch history to do the job.

items.body: Daily images of ice cover in the Arctic Ocean show sea ice melting around the pole from March 15, 2026 to Sept. 12, 2026. Trent Schindler/NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on Sept. 12, according to NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) at the University of Colorado Boulder. The ice covered an estimated 1.78 million square miles (4.6 million square kilometers), tying 2008, 2010, and 2025 for the 10th-lowest minimum in the satellite record. The 2026 minimum is consistent with patterns observed in the satellite record. The past 20 years, from 2007 through 2026, have produced the 20 lowest annual Arctic sea ice minimum extents observed since continuous satellite measurements began in late 1978. Arctic sea ice grows during the dark, cold autumn and winter and retreats as temperatures rise during spring and summer, typically reaching its lowest extent in September. Weather conditions can cause substantial differences in the amount of ice that melts from one summer to another. Lucid—who joined NASA in 1978 as one of its first six female astronauts—checked in on wheat growing in the Svet greenhouse aboard the Russian space station Mir. For six months, Lucid lived and worked alongside two Russian cosmonauts conducting life science studies and other experiments in microgravity. Lucid returned to Earth aboard space shuttle Atlantis on Sept. 26, 1996, completing a 188-day mission—a new record for both a woman and for an American. Lessons from her time on Mir helped NASA prepare for the psychological and cultural challenges of long-duration missions on the International Space Station.   In December 1996, President Bill Clinton awarded Shannon Lucid the Congressional Space Medal of Honor for her achievement. items.title: Long software support matters to smartphone shoppers, poll finds
items.summary: It's a top priority for almost half of you.
items.body: Android phones don’t change much from year to year these days; the Galaxy S26 is extremely similar to the Galaxy S25, which was extremely similar to the Galaxy S24, and so on. That means that, assuming you don’t break it, it’s easier than ever to make a device last. Solid hardware only goes so far, though — long software support matters, too. According to a survey Android Authority ‘s been running, almost all of you agree, rating long-lasting software support as a consideration in choosing your phones. In a poll running for the past couple of weeks, we’ve been asking readers whether long software support is a priority in choosing a new phone. There were three options to choose from: “Yes, it’s a top priority;” “Somewhat, but not a dealbreaker;” or “No, I care more about price.” Just shy of 84% of responses indicated that long software support is indeed a priority.

items.title: I’ve used Razr phones for 20 years, and Motorola’s secret weapon hasn’t changed

The Nokia 5160 I carried around in high school will always hold a special place in my heart, but Motorola soon became my preferred brand. I remember how jealous I was when my parents bought StarTACs. It’s hard to describe what a shift that device was for cell phones. Moto proved that the phones in our pockets could be smaller and more stylish, and the company wasn’t done there. The original Razr was a revelation when it was released in 2004. You didn’t want to buy anything else at the time, and it was hard to go anywhere without seeing someone use one. It’s why Motorola’s recent success isn’t a surprise. The company has maintained a consistent theme over the last two decades, and it doesn’t take much to see where that all began and how it translates perfectly to this current crop of Razrs.

items.title: Google officially opens the door to more games on Android Auto
items.summary: Games on Android Auto and Android Automotive OS are officially out of beta.
items.body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google has officially moved games on Android Auto and Android Automotive OS out of beta and made them generally available. You can already play supported games on your car’s screen while parked by browsing through Google’s collection of games for Android Auto and Android Automotive, but developers can now publish compatible titles to Google Play’s open testing and production tracks. Android Auto and Android Automotive games are blocked while you’re driving for obvious safety reasons. If you’ve ever found yourself sitting in your car with nothing to do, Google is ramping up options for your entertainment. In addition to onboarding video streaming services on Android Auto and Android Automotive, Google is also making in-car gaming a bigger deal this year.
